note: Reference machine: the 2-vCPU cloud container the Day 45 baseline was measured on. Ceilings are roughly 2 to 10 times the measured median, so they catch a real loss, not noise. They are NOT numbers for your laptop or a Raspberry Pi: copy this file to perf/budgets.<name>.json, set "hardware" to the cpu line at the top of your bench output, run scripts/perf/bench.sh there, and set each max from what that machine gives and what a person waiting would accept (see docs/day-45.md).

budgets.why: A committed write (fsync included) must stay far below one 16 ms screen frame so adding a task never feels slow. Measured 0.47 ms here; the fsync of the disk is most of it.
Rebuilding the view from 10,000 ops happens at upgrade and in repair; it must not hold a start-up for half a second. Measured 180 ms.
Catching up 10 new ops is the product-spec catch-up case; its cost must be flat in the size of the log (Day 25). Measured 1.16 ms.
Taking in 1,000 signed ops after a long offline spell must finish well inside a sync round. Measured 87 ms.
A full integrity check of 10,000 ops (offgrid store verify) is run by hand and after upgrades; it must stay a blink. Measured 39 ms.
Every local write allocates this many times; the count does not jitter, so a rise means new work per write. Measured 502.
The cost of one authenticated sync exchange, without the network. Measured 0.58 ms.
Called for every write and every received op; it must stay a few hundred nanoseconds at most. Measured 57 ns.
